Cumulative incidence of the log-logistic distribution

Source: R/ll_cdf.R
ll_cdf.Rd

Computes the cumulative incidence (distribution function) of the log-logistic time-to-event distribution in the parameterization used by Duncan (2026), which is the parameterization of the log-logistic model of the SAS LIFEREG procedure: $$F(t) = 1 - \frac{1}{1 + \exp[(\log t - \mu) / \sigma]}.$$

Usage

ll_cdf(t, mu, sigma)

Arguments

t

Numeric vector of times (positive).

mu

Location (intercept) parameter on the log-time scale.

sigma

Scale parameter (positive). The hazard is decreasing when sigma >= 1 and first increases and then decreases when sigma < 1.

Value

Numeric vector of cumulative incidences. The arguments are recycled to a common length.

References

Duncan, B. (2026). Robust safety monitoring and signal detection using alternatives to the standard Poisson distribution. Journal of Biopharmaceutical Statistics, 36(2), 227–244. doi:10.1080/10543406.2024.2395532

See also

ll_mu

Examples

# incidence at week 104 under the placebo assumption of scenario 6
ll_cdf(104, mu = 7.3, sigma = 0.8)
#> [1] 0.03490787
